rows.old:
Request permissions while OrcaSlicer loads your module.

Each bucket takes the target strings the plugin expects the corresponding audit event to
report: filesystem paths for fs_read and fs_readwrite, URLs for network_http, socket addresses
for network_socket, and commands for process. threading=True requests permission to start
threads. Targets already granted to the plugin are not asked for again.

fs_create and fs_delete take folders rather than files. A literal folder entry grants creating
or deleting entries directly inside that folder, not inside its subfolders. An entry ending in
"/*" is a tree grant: it grants the same for that folder and for every folder below it, at any
depth, for example "/path/to/folder/*". A tree rooted at a filesystem, drive, or network share
root, such as "/*", "C:\\*", or a UNC share root, covers that entire filesystem, drive, or
network share. A relative folder or tree root is
resolved against the working directory when the request is made. Pass "*" on its own for
unrestricted create or delete access; a "*" mixed with other entries is rejected, and a "*"
anywhere other than the final /* of a folder tree is rejected. At runtime, approving a create or
delete prompt stores the parent folder of the approved target as a direct grant, and the prompt
lists that canonical folder; a parent folder whose own name contains "*" is refused rather than
stored. On the main thread the operation then proceeds; a request raised on a worker thread
denies the current operation, so the plugin has to retry it after approval.

A recursive delete (shutil.rmtree) is a subtree operation. A literal folder grant is not
enough, even when it names the target folder or its parent. A saved fs_delete tree grant covers
the entries inside its root; deleting the root folder itself is covered only when the folder
containing that root is also granted. Otherwise the user is asked for one-time consent for the
canonical target subtree before the walk starts. That consent is never saved, covers only that
operation, and a prompt that has to be posted to a worker thread applies to one matching retry
within its short lifetime. Nested deletes inside the approved subtree proceed without another
prompt; denied paths stay blocked. A permission edit, revocation, or reinstall discards any
pending recursive-delete consent, so an old prompt cannot grant access to the reinstalled code.

A filesystem target may end in "/*" to grant a whole directory tree, for example
"/path/to/folder/*". That covers the folder itself and every path beneath it, at any depth.
"*" is the only wildcard and is recognized only as the final path component; a "*" anywhere
else in a target is an ordinary character. Tree grants apply to fs_read, fs_readwrite,
fs_create and fs_delete, and a grant in one bucket never authorizes another direction. For
fs_delete, the tree covers deleting entries inside the folder and below, not deleting the
folder root itself; that removal needs the parent folder granted. Tree
grants are matched on canonical paths, so a symlink below the granted folder does not extend
the grant outside it. Paths the host denies by name or keyword stay denied even when a
wildcard covers them.

`network` also lists http(s) URLs, but each is reduced to its scheme and host, so one grant covers
every path, query and port on that host and also authorizes raw socket events for it. The host
presents one request to the user after register_capabilities() returns and before any capability
instance is created. Denying the request aborts the plugin load.

rows.old:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.

rows.old:
Enable full access for "%s"?

Full access turns off permission auditing for this plugin: its file system, network, process, thread and event permissions are no longer checked. The plugin can read and write most files your user account can access, including startup scripts, SSH keys and a writable OrcaSlicer installation. Modifying startup or application files can let code run outside these checks. Direct Python access to OrcaSlicer's configuration, secret, certificate and install-state paths stays blocked, but subprocesses are not restricted. Full access is not a sandbox.

Only enable this for a plugin you trust.
rows.new:
Enable full access for "%s"?

Full access turns off permission auditing for this plugin: its file system, network, process, thread and event permissions are no longer checked. The plugin can read and write most files your user account can access, including startup scripts, SSH keys and a writable CosmoSlice installation. Modifying startup or application files can let code run outside these checks. Direct Python access to CosmoSlice's configuration, secret, certificate and install-state paths stays blocked, but subprocesses are not restricted. Full access is not a sandbox.

Only enable this for a plugin you trust.

rows.old:
Force the toolhead to travel to the wipe tower before issuing the tool change command (Tx).

Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. By default Orca skips the travel on multi-toolhead machines because the firmware handles the head swap, which can result in the Tx command being issued above the printed part. Enable this option if you want the tool change to always be issued above the wipe tower instead.

rows.old:
This option sets the max point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. OrcaSlicer ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer.

The default setting is (99999, 99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

rows.old:
To use OrcaSlicer with Bambu Lab printers, you need to enable LAN mode and Developer mode on your printer.

Please go to your printer's settings and:
1. Turn on LAN mode
2. Enable Developer mode

Developer mode allows the printer to work exclusively through local network access, enabling full functionality with OrcaSlicer.

To use CosmoSlice with Bambu Lab printers, you need to enable LAN mode and Developer mode on your printer.

Please go to your printer's settings and:
1. Turn on LAN mode
2. Enable Developer mode

Developer mode allows the printer to work exclusively through local network access, enabling full functionality with CosmoSlice.
